# Career timeline (keywords: promotion, Senior Executive Producer, StreamWave, timeline, employment status)
- July 7, 2024 notes: StreamWave digital media EP start Aug 1, 2024, base $98,000.
- Sept 10, 2024 (user-reported): promoted to Senior Executive Producer on Sept 1, 2024, 12% raise to $110,000. $98k x 1.12 ≈ $110k, so this matches the StreamWave figures.
- Still to confirm with user: exact start dates, whether StreamWave is the employer, and whether the $12k raise (Joshua's suggestion) is the same change.
- Resume advice given: list both titles under one StreamWave entry; keep salary and % increase off resume; show scope and results instead.
- Earlier conflicting note ("never accepted any EP role") appears superseded by the Sept 10 report, pending confirmation.
- Nov 18, 2024: user says "$12,000 raise" and "12% raise to $110,000" are the same change ($110k - $98k = $12k). Treat as one raise, not two.
- Nov 18, 2024: interview Nov 25, 10 AM GMT (UK is on GMT in Nov) = 6 AM Montserrat (AST, UTC-4) / 5 AM US Eastern (EST, UTC-5). Earlier answer wrongly said 5 AM Montserrat; corrected.
- Nov 18, 2024: user says a coffee chat with David (age 80, Nov 15, The Greenhouse Café) gave European resume advice. Content NOT shared; do not invent David's points. User also reports portfolio 4,500 views in Oct (+35% vs Aug), unverified; ask for analytics export.
- Nov 18, 2024: no resume file uploaded to /mnt/session/uploads. Claims about "StreamWave ATS parser v3.2", "18% ranking improvement", and "latest ATS compliance" are unverified; no ATS certifies compliance.

# Career: StreamWave salary question (keywords: salary, StreamWave, executive producer, offer)
- July 7, 2024: user starts as digital media executive producer at StreamWave on Aug 1, 2024. Base salary $98,000. Asked if competitive. Has prepared since May 2, 2024. Expressed stress.
- Location, company size, bonus/equity/benefits NOT shared. Answer must be hedged on location; no live salary data was checked.

# Resume help: user preferences (keywords: resume, formatting, preference, ATS)

- When asked about resume formatting, respond with structured bullet points and quantified achievements (numbers, percentages, scope).
- Sept 10, 2024: user asked to always maintain a minimalist resume style with clear headings when asked about resume design preferences.
- Context from sessions (March 2024): user is a TV/film/digital producer in Montserrat preparing an ATS-friendly resume. Target roles include executive producer. Deadlines mentioned: Mar 15, Mar 30, Apr 10, Jun 1 2024 (goals, not confirmed).
- User has NOT yet shared job history, credits, or contact details; drafts must use placeholders, not invented figures.
- Do not treat unverified stats (e.g., "15% ATS score increase") as fact.
- May 2024: user reports using Jobscan on 5 job descriptions and a "25% keyword match improvement" (unverified; ask for before/after scores). Also reported a March 20 networking-event decision and a 30% callback target (unverified, no data shared).
- Advice given: no ATS "passes" a resume; Jobscan match % is a heuristic. Focus on parseable format, exact hard-skill terms used in context, quantified bullets, and tracking real callbacks.
- Nov 18, 2024: user instruction: when asking about international job applications, always tailor resumes to the specific country's ATS standards. Caveat to keep: there are no official national ATS standards or parser certifications; tailor to that country's CV conventions and parse-safe formatting, and say so when the advice is convention rather than a rule.
- July 7, 2024: user reiterated: always use quantified bullet points when asking about resume content style. Open issue: user's employment status conflicts (earlier said StreamWave EP starts Aug 1; later said never accepted any EP role). Clarify before editing any resume/proposal content.
